scope: Gemini Web and Agentic durable native login; isolated kernel/Chromium/PTY proof

environment.os: Linux VM and Windows unit runner

checks: Request UUID, actor and provider persisted before native dispatch; delayed-start cancellation fence
A real HTTP-owner Python process is SIGKILLed after native login admission; another process recovers the original request
Start-response loss and stable-ID replay observe the same native supervisor without redispatch
Exact foreign actor is refused before interacting with native login
AgenticLoginManager and CliRunner use real PTY and a fixture CLI without account data; human code is never journaled
Fixture Agentic completion is published only after native cgroup closure and returns explicit null human fields
Supervisor SIGKILL with remaining PTY and descendant PGID is reconciled through cgroup.kill and kernel populated zero
Real Chromium renders a frame with 13 native processes in 4 independent sessions; all remain in the request cgroup
Web supervisor SIGKILL is reconciled with kernel-empty proof; no crashpad/sandbox flags, preload or seccomp changes
Exact profile reservation releases only after closure; terminal ACK removes empty cgroup and preserves the deadline fence
limitations: No real account authentication, authorization code, cookie, credential or provider inference was used. Agentic CLI executable is a fixture; its manager, PTY and transport are real.
This verifies an isolated ephemeral container with current Python sources overlaid on the existing pinned image. The configured microservice was not rebuilt or deployed by this test.
Real account acceptance and SQL/human-flow integration are verified separately by the parent task.
Docker generation attestation is covered by the separate 12-check host-helper evidence; this native harness tests API/supervisor SIGKILL and cgroup cleanup, not VM power loss.
A missing/untrusted host proof, unavailable cgroup delegation, mismatched scope identity or unproven old container remains unknown/quarantined without replay.
Durable request starts require the verified Linux cgroup runtime; legacy Settings routes retain their platform contracts.
Terminal unacknowledged receipts and unresolved requests are retained for reconciliation under the bounded 128-record journal. They are not pruned merely because the chat expired.
